Subject: Solstice MAP: execution plan for long-context performance validation

Hi Lisa / Ravi —

Thanks for the deep dive call earlier. Per our discussion, I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan that focuses on the performance validation you asked for: long-context behavior (up to 32k tokens), time-to-first-token (TTFT), steady-state throughput, and concurrency headroom with and without KV cache warmed.

Key asks from Solstice (recap):
- Validate TTFT and P50/P95/P99 token latencies on your top-3 prompt distributions.
- Estimate sustained throughput at 8, 16, and 32 concurrent sessions.
- Demonstrate KV cache hit/miss delta for multi-turn workflows (typical session length ~6 turns).
- Surface failure modes and fallback behavior for sequences > 16k.

Attached: solstice_map_draft_v1.pdf — contains milestones, success criteria, and test harness plan.

Proposed immediate next steps:
1) You share one week of anonymized prompt-size distribution (or sample prompts) by EOD Monday.
2) Our infra team runs two baseline sweeps (cold KV, warm KV) and returns a perf bundle with traces.
3) We review in a canary review session and sign off on the production rollout criteria.

Can you confirm the sample data share and whether you have a preferred NDA/POC clause we should include in the MAP?

Thanks,
Grace

Grace —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifying points before we share sample prompts:
1) For TTFT, do you measure from HTTP request arrival to first token byte on a streaming socket, or to the first character returned in the API response body? We need the same definition for internal benchmarks.
2) What does "warm KV" mean operationally for Redwood? Is that per-session prefix caching or global prefix caching? Our sessions share a common system prompt but also have unique user messages.
3) We cannot share raw PHI-containing prompts. We'll provide synthetically redacted examples that preserve tokenization and length distribution.

Finally — are there any SLOs you commit to in the MAP for P95 latency under 1s for sequences <8k? We need to understand realistic expectations for our latency budget.

Best,
Lisa Chen
Director, ML Platforms
Solstice Health
lisa.chen@solstice.health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@solstice.health>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-26T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solstice MAP: execution plan for long-context performance validation

Lisa —

Quick answers:
- TTFT definition: we report both measurements. Primary metric used in MAP = request arrival -> first byte on streaming socket (TTFT_stream). We also include time-to-first-API-response (TTFR_http). We'll label both in the CSV.

- Warm KV definition: two modes in our tests:
  * per-session warm: KV cache populated from the first N-turns of the same session (models with KV caching keep per-request KV entries on the serving node); this simulates a returning user.
  * global prefix warm: common system prompts/prefixes are preloaded into a shared prefix cache so first turn benefits.

Test harness outline (executed by Redwood infra team):
- Models: curated open checkpoint (r-infer-large) and a quantized high-throughput variant (r-infer-large-q4).
- Sequence lengths tested: 2k, 8k, 16k, 32k max tokens. Prompt-size distribution buckets from your sample (we'll mirror).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 16, 32 sessions. Each session runs 100 two-turn dialogues (avg 6 user turns total across the test).
- Metrics collected: TTFT_stream, P50/P95/P99 token latency, tokens/sec throughput, memory footprint, GPU util, KV hit rate, and error/retry counts.

Attached for visibility: solstice_perf_results_v1.csv (raw numbers from a representative run) and kvcache-sample-traces.json (trace snippets showing KV hits/misses).

Preliminary callouts from the baseline run (summary):
- 2k sequences: P95 token latency 0.42s, TTFT_stream median 0.18s at concurrency=8 (warm KV).
- 8k sequences: P95 token latency 0.9s, TTFT_stream median 0.28s at concurrency=8 (warm KV).
- 16k sequences: P95 token latency 1.9s, TTFT_stream median 0.55s at concurrency=8 (cold KV).
- 32k sequences: sustained throughput drops ~45% vs 8k; P99 spikes and we observed transient mem-pressure triggered re-queueing in ~0.7% of requests at concurrency=32.

KV cache impact (approx): warming per-session KV reduced P95 by ~18% for multi-turn scenarios on 8k/16k tests. Global prefix warm produced smaller but consistent improvements (~6-8%) for first-turn response.

I realize these are raw numbers; for the MAP we'll provide labeled CSVs and a short explainer deck that maps these metrics to success criteria.

-Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Solstice MAP: execution plan for long-context performance validation

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from platform engineering:
- Can you add a TTFT P90 and show distributions rather than only percentiles? We want to see the tail shape.
- For the 32k tests, what memory configuration (GPU type / vram) were you using and what quantization profile? We are particularly sensitive to model artifacts when quantized to Q4.
- For the re-queueing you saw at concurrency=32, was that an application-level retry or built into the serving runtime?

Also, can we map the MAP milestones to calendar dates? Our leadership wants a 6-week timeline from kick-off to production canary.

Ravi
Senior Platform Engineer
Solstice Health
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-03T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Solstice MAP: execution plan for long-context performance validation

Ravi / Lisa —

We can do a six-week MAP. Draft timeline below with owners and acceptance criteria. I've put the full schedule in the attached MAP doc (and the Google Doc link).

Week 0 (kick-off) — agree success criteria, share redacted prompt samples (owner: Solstice)
Week 1 — baseline runs (cold/warm KV) and CSV delivery (owner: Redwood perf team)
Week 2 — follow-up runs with quantization profile adjustments (owner: Redwood infra)
Week 3 — failure-mode stress tests (concurrency=32+, simulated network jitter) (owner: Redwood infra)
Week 4 — performance tuning and optimizations (batching, kernel selection, quantization) (owner: Redwood + Solstice)
Week 5 — production canary plan, rollback criteria, runbook (owner: Redwood + Solstice)
Week 6 — production canary (owner: Solstice ops with Redwood support)

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- P95 token latency < 1.2s for sequences <= 8k at concurrency=16 with warm KV
- TTFT_stream median < 0.35s for sequences <= 8k
- KV hit rate > 70% for repeated-session traffic in the canary profile
- No more than 0.5% re-queue/retry events in steady-state at concurrency=32

Deliverables: MAP sign-off, perf CSVs, trace bundle, canary runbook, and a short sync to executive sponsors.

If this looks good, Grace — can you confirm dates for kick-off next Monday and we will send calendar invites?

Thanks,
Tessa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Lisa/Ravi —

Confirmed. Kick-off Monday 2027-05-10 at 10:00am PT. I'll send the calendar hold and the updated MAP (signed by Redwood) after I get your redacted samples.

Quick note on the quantization config from our table: the baseline r-infer-large-q4 run uses per-tensor 4-bit quantization with selective FP16 attention kernels. GPU used: A100 80GB for 16/32k runs, and A10G for 2k/8k microbenchmarks. We'll include exact node images and kernel tags in the CSV metadata.

Attachments: solstice_map_draft_v1.pdf, solstice_perf_results_v1.csv, kvcache-sample-traces.json

See you Monday.

Grace
